subtitle_zh: 一场大雨以后，她决定说真话
title_en: The Girl Who Went Back to the Village
subtitle_en: After the storm, she chose to tell the truth
author: Text and translation by Claude (Anthropic)

segs.en: The year she turned twenty-eight, Lin Xia made a decision that surprised everyone: she quit her job, left Shenzhen and went back to her family home in the mountains of Fujian.
It was a small tea-growing village not far from the Wuyi Mountains, and for generations its people had lived from tea.
As more and more young people left to work in the cities, the village grew quieter every year; those who stayed were mostly old people and children.
tok: to work as a migrant worker

segs.en: When Lin Xia left home at eighteen, she thought she would never come back.

zh: 林夏二十八岁那年，做了一个让所有人都吃惊的决定：她辞职离开了深圳，回到了福建山里的老家。那是一个种茶的小村子，离武夷山不远，村里的人祖祖辈辈都靠茶叶生活。随着越来越多的年轻人去城市打工，村子一年比一年安静，留在村里的大多是老人和孩子。林夏十八岁离开家的时候，以为自己再也不会回来了。

segs.en: Quitting

zh: 辞职

segs.en: In Shenzhen, Lin Xia worked in marketing for a company. She left home at eight every morning and did not get back until ten at night.
Her income was not low, but the rent was high too, and by the end of each month she could hardly save anything.
One night, after working late, she stood alone in a subway station and suddenly felt terribly tired.
She thought of the tea gardens back home: the white clouds on the hills in the morning, the birds singing in the woods, and the fragrance that filled the house whenever her father made tea.

zh: 在深圳，林夏在一家公司做市场工作，每天早上八点出门，晚上十点才回家。她的收入不低，可是房租也很贵，一个月下来，几乎存不下钱。有一天晚上，她加班到很晚，一个人站在地铁站里，突然觉得特别累。她想起了老家的茶园：早上山上的白云，树林里的鸟叫，还有爸爸做茶的时候满屋子的茶香。

segs.en: That night she phoned her mother.
“Mum, I want to come home.”
Her mother paused. “For New Year? That's still a long way off.”
“No. I want to quit my job and come back to the village to sell tea.”
The other end of the line was silent for a long time.
At last her mother said quietly, “As for your father… you'll have to tell him yourself.”

zh: 那天晚上，她给妈妈打了一个电话。“妈，我想回家。”妈妈停了一下：“回来过年？还早呢。”“不是，我想辞职，回村里卖茶。”电话那头安静了很久。最后，妈妈小声说：“你爸那边……你自己跟他说吧。”

segs.en: Lin Xia's colleagues did not understand either.
“Even if you're not happy in Shenzhen, there's no need to go back to the countryside, is there?” said one colleague. “Once you go back, it's very hard to come back again.”
Lin Xia just smiled and said nothing.
In fact she was afraid too, but she had thought it through: these days lots of people buy things online, and farm produce can be sold online as well.
She had worked in marketing for several years and knew a little about promotion, so why not give it a try?
Although she was not at all sure of herself, she still handed in her resignation letter.

zh: 林夏的同事们也不理解。“即使你在深圳过得不开心，也用不着回农村吧？”一个同事说，“一旦回去了，就很难再回来了。”林夏笑了笑，没有回答。其实她也害怕，可是她已经想好了：现在很多人在网上买东西，农产品也可以在网上卖。她做了好几年市场，懂一点儿宣传，为什么不试试呢？尽管心里一点儿把握也没有，她还是交上了辞职信。

segs.en: Father's Silence

zh: 爸爸的沉默

segs.en: On the day Lin Xia arrived home, her father was in the courtyard mending a bamboo basket.
When he saw his daughter walk in pulling two big suitcases, he only glanced up, said, “You're back,” and went back to mending his basket.
At dinner her mother cooked a whole table of dishes. Lin Xia talked a lot about Shenzhen, and about her plans.
Her father said nothing the whole time; he just drank cup after cup of tea.

zh: 林夏回到家那天，爸爸正在院子里修竹筐。看见女儿拉着两个大箱子走进来，他只抬头看了一眼，说了一句“回来了”，就又接着修他的竹筐了。晚饭的时候，妈妈做了一桌子菜，林夏说了很多深圳的事，也说了自己的计划。爸爸一直没有说话，只是一杯一杯地喝茶。

segs.en: When the meal was over, her father put down his cup and finally spoke. “Your mother and I worked ourselves to the bone to put you through university, just so you wouldn't have to live the way we do. And look at you: you've come running back.”
“Dad, things are different now. You can build a career in the village too.”
“What career?” Her father's voice was low. “What will people in the village say? That Old Lin's daughter couldn't make it in the city and had no choice but to come home.”
With that, he stood up and went into his room.

zh: 吃完饭，爸爸放下杯子，终于说话了：“我和你妈辛辛苦苦挣钱让你读大学，就是希望你别再过我们这样的日子。你倒好，自己跑回来了。”“爸，现在不一样了，在村里也能做事业。”“什么事业？”爸爸的声音很低，“村里人会怎么说？说老林的女儿在城里待不下去，只好回家。”说完，他站起来，走进了自己的房间。

segs.en: That night Lin Xia lay awake for a long time.
Her mother came in quietly and sat on the edge of the bed.

“Don't blame your father. Even though he doesn't say it, he still cares about you more than anyone.” Her mother's voice was soft. “After all, he's grown tea his whole life; he knows how hard this work is.”
“Mum, I'm not afraid of hard work.”
“I know. But unless you really make something of it, he won't change his mind.”
Lin Xia looked out at the dark mountains and said to herself: I'm going to make him see.

zh: 那天晚上，林夏很久都睡不着。妈妈轻轻地走进来，坐在床边。“你别怪你爸。尽管他嘴上不说，心里还是比谁都在乎你。”妈妈轻轻地说，“毕竟他种了一辈子茶，知道这一行有多苦。”“妈，我不怕苦。”“我知道。可是除非你真做出点儿样子来，否则他是不会改变看法的。”林夏看着窗外黑黑的山，心里对自己说：我一定要让他看到。

segs.en: The Live Stream Nobody Watched

zh: 没人看的直播

segs.en: The very next day, Lin Xia began to get ready.
She opened a little online shop, and bought a phone stand and a small light.
Her plan was simple: stream live from the tea garden every day, let viewers see how tea is grown, picked and made, and then sell the family's tea.
Lin Xia's primary school classmate A Jie ran a parcel delivery point at the entrance to the village.
When he heard she was going to sell tea online, he thumped his chest and said, “As long as there are orders, leave the shipping to me!”

zh: 第二天，林夏就开始准备了。她在网上开了一家小店，又买了一个手机支架和一个小灯。她的计划很简单：每天在茶园里直播，让观众看看茶是怎么种、怎么摘、怎么做的，再把家里的茶卖出去。林夏的小学同学阿杰在村口开了一个快递点。听说她要在网上卖茶，他拍着胸口说：“只要有订单，发货的事包在我身上！”

segs.en: But the very first stream ran into trouble.
The tea garden was halfway up the mountain, and unless you climbed to the very top, there was hardly any phone signal.
Whenever the signal dropped, the picture would freeze one moment and cut out the next.
Lin Xia talked to her phone for an hour, and there were never more than three people in the stream; one of them was A Jie.
The second and third times were much the same.

zh: 可是第一次直播就出了问题。茶园在半山上，除非走到山上最高的地方，否则手机几乎没有信号。信号一旦不好，画面就一会儿卡住，一会儿断掉。林夏对着手机讲了一个小时，直播间里最多只有三个人，其中一个还是阿杰。第二次、第三次也差不多。

segs.en: One day, a viewer she didn't know finally turned up in the stream.
Lin Xia was delighted. She quickly greeted him and started telling him about her family's tea.
But all he left was one line: “This expensive? Who knows if it's real rock tea?” And then he was gone.
Lin Xia stared at her phone and could not say a word for a long while.

zh: 有一天，直播间里终于来了一个不认识的观众。林夏高兴极了，赶紧向他问好，给他介绍家里的茶。可是那个人只留下了一句话：“这么贵，谁知道是不是真的岩茶？”然后就离开了。林夏看着手机，半天说不出话来。

segs.en: A month went by and Lin Xia had sold only seven boxes of tea, and five of those were bought by her friends in Shenzhen.
People in the village began to gossip.
Once she heard two neighbours chatting by the road. “Young people these days think it's all so simple. Talk to your phone a bit and you can sell tea?”
“Exactly. Old Lin's daughter studied all those years, and in the end she's back to farming.”
When she got home that evening, her father glanced at her and said nothing.
But his silence hurt her more than criticism would have.

zh: 一个月过去了，林夏只卖出去七盒茶，其中五盒还是她在深圳的朋友买的。村里开始有人说闲话。有一次，她听见两个邻居在路边聊天：“现在的年轻人想得太简单了，对着手机说说话，就能把茶卖出去？”“就是，老林家的女儿读了那么多书，最后还是回来种地了。”那天晚上回到家，爸爸看了她一眼，什么也没说。可是他的沉默比批评更让她难受。

segs.en: She thought about giving up, too.
On several nights she opened a job website and looked through one Shenzhen position after another, for a long time, before closing it.
But the next morning she still climbed the mountain with her phone and stand on her back.
Although she was tired every day and hardly anyone watched, she still kept streaming for two hours a day.
She moved her streaming spot higher up, where the signal was a little better, and learned from online videos how to talk to the camera and how to frame a shot.
She told herself, “Even if only one person is watching today, I'm going to do it properly.”

zh: 她也想过放弃。有好几个晚上，她打开找工作的网站，看着深圳的一个个职位，看了很久才关上。可是第二天早上，她还是背着手机和支架上了山。尽管每天都很累，看的人也很少，她还是坚持每天直播两个小时。她把直播的地方搬到了信号好一点儿的高处，又跟着网上的视频学习怎么说话、怎么拍画面。她对自己说：“即使今天只有一个人看，我也要好好讲。”

segs.en: A Great Storm

zh: 一场大雨

segs.en: At the end of April, the village began picking tea.
This is the most important time of the year: most of the villagers' income for the whole year depends on the spring tea.
Every day, as soon as it was light, the tea farmers set off up the mountain with bamboo baskets on their backs.
Her father always said that picking tea depends on the weather: once the leaves miss their best moment, they grow old, and the tea made from them tastes much worse.

zh: 四月底，村里开始采茶了。这是一年里最重要的时候，村里人一年的收入，大部分都靠春茶。每天天刚亮，茶农们就背着竹筐上山了。爸爸常说，采茶要看天气，叶子一旦错过了最好的时间，就会变老，做出来的茶味道也差多了。

segs.en: But on the third day of picking, the weather suddenly changed.
In the afternoon the sun was still blazing, but as night fell, black clouds came rolling in from behind the mountain.
Then a heavy rain began to fall, and the wind grew stronger and stronger.
It rained for three whole days and nights, and the little river outside the village rose to the brim.
Even on the night of the heaviest rain, her father put on his raincoat, took a lamp and went up the mountain to check on the tea garden.
Her mother couldn't talk him out of it, so she stood in the doorway and waited until he came back soaked to the skin.

zh: 可就在采茶的第三天，天气突然变了。下午还是大太阳，天快黑的时候，黑云从山那边压了过来。接着，下起了大雨，风也越来越大。雨整整下了三天三夜，村子外面的小河涨得满满的。即使是雨最大的那个晚上，爸爸也穿上雨衣，拿着灯上山去看茶园。妈妈劝不住他，只好站在门口等，一直等到他全身湿透地回来。

segs.en: When the rain stopped, Lin Xia followed her father up the mountain.

What she saw left her speechless: the new leaves on many of the tea bushes had been beaten off, a large stretch of soil in one garden had been washed away, and several old tea bushes lay toppled in the muddy water.
Her father crouched down and propped one bush back up with his hands, and for a long time he did not stand up.
“This year's spring tea,” he said, “there's half of it left at most.”
Lin Xia had never heard her father speak in such a quiet voice.

zh: 雨停以后，林夏跟着爸爸上了山。眼前的样子让她说不出话来：很多茶树新长出来的叶子都被打掉了，一块茶园的土被雨水冲走了一大片，几棵老茶树倒在泥水里。爸爸蹲下去，用手把一棵茶树扶起来，半天都没有站起来。“今年的春茶，最多只剩一半了。”他说。林夏从来没听过爸爸用这么轻的声音说话。

segs.en: On the way home, neither of them said a word.
Lin Xia knew what this meant: with half the tea gone, the family's income for the year would be cut by more than half.
What's more, leaves picked after rain hold too much water, and it is hard to make good tea from them.
That evening she opened her computer, meaning to write some promotional copy.
Like everyone else, she wrote: “This year's spring tea: exceptional quality, limited stock, buy now!”
But as she wrote, she stopped.
It wasn't true.
She didn't want to deceive anyone, least of all the people who were willing to trust her.

zh: 回家的路上，两个人谁也没有说话。林夏知道这意味着什么：茶少了一半，家里这一年的收入就少了一大半。而且雨后摘的叶子水分太多，很难做出好茶。晚上，她打开电脑，想写一段宣传的话。像别人一样，她写下：“今年春茶，品质特别好，数量有限，欢迎购买！”可是写着写着，她停了下来。这不是真的。她不想骗人，更不想骗那些愿意相信她的人。

segs.en: Telling the Truth

zh: 说真话

segs.en: The next morning, Lin Xia did not prepare what she would say; she took her phone straight to the tea garden the rain had wrecked.
“Hello, everyone. I'm not selling tea today,” she said to the camera. “I want to show you our village's tea gardens.”
She pointed the camera at the fallen bushes, the washed-away soil, and the villagers who were propping the bushes back up one by one.
“The heavy rain of the last few days has cost us half of this year's spring tea. My father has grown tea for forty years, and I've never seen him so upset.”

zh: 第二天早上，林夏没有提前准备要说的话，直接把手机带到了被雨冲坏的茶园。“大家好，今天我不卖茶。”她对着镜头说，“我想让大家看看我们村的茶园。”她把镜头对着倒下的茶树、被冲走的土，还有正在一棵一棵扶茶树的村民。“这几天的大雨，让我们今年的春茶少了一半。我爸爸种了四十年茶，我从来没见过他这么难过。”

segs.en: She paused, then went on. “I know a lot of people worry about buying fake tea online. So I want to be clear with you: tea picked after the rain is lower in quality, and I won't sell it as good tea.”

“Unless it was picked before the rain and made by my father himself, it won't go into my shop. There isn't much good tea this year, and it won't be cheap, but I promise you every box is the real thing.”
When she had finished, her eyes were a little red.

zh: 她停了一下，又说：“我知道很多人担心在网上买到假茶。所以我想跟大家说清楚：雨后摘的茶，质量会差一些，我不会把它们当好茶卖。”“除非是下雨以前摘的、我爸爸自己做的茶，否则我不会放进我的店里。今年的好茶不多，价格也不会便宜，但是我保证，每一盒都是真的。”说完这些话，她的眼睛有点儿红了。

segs.en: That day there were far more people in the stream than ever before, and more kept coming.
Someone commented, “This is the most honest live stream I've ever seen.”
Someone else wrote, “My family grew tea when I was little. This made me cry.”
And another: “I don't mind paying a bit more. I just want the real thing.”
Lin Xia read the comments one by one. She didn't know what to say, and could only say “thank you” over and over.

zh: 那天直播间里的人比以前多了很多，而且越来越多。有人评论说：“这是我看过的最真实的直播。”有人说：“我小时候家里也种茶，看哭了。”还有人说：“贵一点儿没关系，我就要真的。”林夏一条一条地看着，不知道该说什么，只能一遍一遍地说“谢谢”。

segs.en: An hour later A Jie phoned, his voice quite changed. “Xiaxia, look at your phone, quick! There are too many orders, I can't possibly handle them on my own!”
That day Lin Xia sold more than three hundred boxes of tea, dozens of times more than in the whole of the previous month.
Over the next few days the orders kept on coming.
As the orders piled up, a few young people from the village were brought in to help with packing and shipping.
One viewer even wrote to say the tea had arrived and was exactly as described in the stream.

zh: 一个小时以后，阿杰打来电话，声音都变了：“夏夏，你快看看手机！订单太多了，我一个人根本忙不过来！”那一天，林夏卖出了三百多盒茶，比过去一个月加起来多了几十倍。后来的几天，订单还在不断地来。随着订单越来越多，村里几个年轻人也被请来帮忙包装和发货。有一个观众还写信来说：茶收到了，跟直播里说的一模一样。

segs.en: In the evening, many viewers were still sending Lin Xia messages.
One question came up again and again: “How is real rock tea made? Can you show us?”
Looking at these questions, Lin Xia had an idea.
But she knew this was something she couldn't do herself.
In the whole village, there was only one person who could really explain it.

zh: 晚上，很多观众还在给林夏发消息。其中有一个问题被问了很多次：“真正的岩茶是怎么做出来的？能不能让我们看看？”林夏看着这些问题，心里有了一个主意。可是她知道，这件事她自己做不了。全村能把这个问题讲清楚的，只有一个人。

segs.en: Father in Front of the Camera

zh: 镜头前的爸爸

segs.en: “I'm not doing it.” Her father shook his head the moment he heard. “Talking to a phone, what does that look like!”
“Dad, people want to know how real rock tea is made. I only know a little about it. You're the one who really understands it.”
Her father didn't answer; he turned away to check the charcoal fire in the roasting room.
Lin Xia didn't press him any further.
She knew that once her father had made up his mind, no one could talk him round.

zh: “我不去。”爸爸听完，马上摇头，“对着手机说话，像什么样子！”“爸，大家想知道真正的岩茶是怎么做出来的。这些我只懂一点儿，只有你真正懂。”爸爸没有回答，转身去看焙房里的炭火。林夏没有再劝他。她知道，爸爸决定了的事，谁劝也没有用。

segs.en: But the next evening, just as Lin Xia started the stream, her father walked into the roasting room.
He had changed into a clean shirt, and his hair was neatly combed.
Although he had said he wouldn't come, in the end he came all the same.
“Go on, film,” he said, sitting a little stiffly beside the roasting basket. “But I'll only talk about making tea, nothing else.”

zh: 可是第二天晚上，林夏刚打开直播，爸爸就走进了焙房。他换了一件干净的衬衫，头发也整整齐齐的。尽管他嘴上说不来，最后他还是来了。“你拍吧。”他有点儿不自然地坐在焙笼旁边，“不过我只讲做茶，别的不讲。”

segs.en: Once he started talking about tea, her father seemed like a different man.
He told the viewers that after rock tea is picked, it must first be dried in the sun, then shaken, then pan-fired, then rolled, and not a single step can be skipped.
Last of all, it has to be slowly roasted over charcoal.
tok: to roast over a low fire

segs.en: “If the fire's too hot, the tea is ruined; if it's too low, the tea isn't fragrant enough. One roasting takes a dozen hours or more, and someone has to keep watch through the night.”
tok: to roast over a low fire

segs.en: As he spoke he tested the heat of the charcoal with his hand, as gently as if he were looking after a child.

zh: 一旦讲起茶来，爸爸就像变了一个人。他告诉观众，岩茶摘下来以后，要先晒，再摇，再炒，再揉，一步也不能少。最后，还要用炭火慢慢地焙。“火大了，茶就坏了；火小了，茶又不够香。一焙就是十几个小时，晚上也得有人守着。”他一边说，一边用手试了试炭火的温度，那样子，就像在照顾一个孩子。

segs.en: A viewer asked him, “Master Lin, isn't it exhausting, making tea like this?”
Her father laughed. “Of course it is. But that's what making tea is like; you can't hurry it. Good tea is something you pay for with time.”
After a moment he added, “People are the same.”
As he said it, he glanced at his daughter.

zh: 有观众问他：“林师傅，这样做茶累不累？”爸爸笑了：“累啊。可是做茶就是这样，急不得。好茶是用时间换来的。”过了一会儿，他又说：“人也一样。”说这句话的时候，他看了女儿一眼。

segs.en: From then on, her father appeared in the stream almost every evening.
The viewers all called him “Master Lin”, and many people came just to hear him talk about tea.
Not only did they buy tea, they began asking whether they could come to the village and see the tea gardens for themselves.
By the autumn, several other households in the village had come to Lin Xia asking her to help sell their tea.
The county also sent someone to look into things, and promised to help the village fix its network.
After all, if a village is going to develop, one person alone is not enough.

zh: 从那以后，爸爸几乎每天晚上都出现在直播里。观众们都叫他“林师傅”，很多人专门来听他讲茶。他们不但买茶，而且开始问能不能到村里来，自己看看茶园。到了秋天，村里另外几户人家也来找林夏，请她帮忙卖茶。县里也派人来了解情况，说要帮村里把网络修好。毕竟，一个村子要发展，光靠一个人是不够的。

segs.en: One evening, after the stream was over, father and daughter sat in the courtyard drinking tea.
“Xiaxia,” her father said suddenly, “when you first came back, I thought you'd come home because you had failed out there. I was wrong.”
Lin Xia had never expected her father to say this; after a moment she smiled. “Dad, even if you'd never said it, I'd still know you were looking out for me.”
Her father took a sip of tea and said, “Making tea is something you can only do your whole life if you truly love it. And from what I can see, you truly do.”
A gentle breeze came down from the mountain, and the scent of tea drifted slowly out of the roasting room.
The city might be big, Lin Xia thought, but this was the place where she wanted to stay.

zh: 一个晚上，直播结束以后，爸爸和林夏坐在院子里喝茶。“夏夏，”爸爸忽然说，“你刚回来的时候，我以为你是在外面失败了才回来的。是我想错了。”林夏没想到爸爸会说这些，过了一会儿才笑了：“爸，即使你不说，我也知道你是关心我。”爸爸喝了一口茶，又说：“做茶这件事，除非你真的喜欢，才能做一辈子。我看你，是真的喜欢。”山上的风轻轻地吹着，茶香从焙房里慢慢地传出来。林夏想，城市虽然很大，可是这里，才是她想留下来的地方。
